thread:
Mia: Quick heads-up — after today's poetry lock refresh CI started failing for model-serving. Snyk flagged a tokenizer CVE and the tests are segfaulting on import. https://snyk.io/vuln/CVE-2026-XXXX
Sanjay: which job is failing? can you paste the failing log snippet?
Mia: unit-tests + docker build. main error: `ImportError` -> segfault inside `tokenizers` wheel when loading `AutoTokenizer`. Short log: `Abort trap: 6` during `pytest tests/inference/test_endtoend.py::test_gpt_inference`
Jordan: ugh. sounds like the 0.12.x tokenizers ABI change bit us. Did dependabot bump `tokenizers` in the lock?
Kevin: yes — dependabot PR #432 updated `poetry.lock` and bumped `transformers` and `tokenizers`. I approved yesterday but didn't run the full macOS/arm matrix.
Mia: we need to triage CVE vs CI break separately but both urgent. Immediate ask: can we revert the lockfile to unblock CI and then apply a constrained upgrade with a verified patched version?
Sanjay: propose rollback plan: 1) revert `poetry.lock` to commit `a1b2c3` (pre-bump); 2) add constraint in `pyproject.toml` like `tokenizers = "<0.12,>=0.11.3"` and `transformers = "<4.35,>=4.33"`; 3) open a hotfix PR that runs full test matrix; 4) block dependabot updates to those packages until we confirm patched wheels.
Jordan: also add a short checklist: run inference perf + quantization tests because ABI changes can subtly alter behavior. And run our eval prompt sets for regressions.
Kevin: I'll prepare the rollback PR. Repro steps I used locally:
```
git checkout a1b2c3 -- poetry.lock
poetry install --no-root
pytest -k inference -q
```
On macOS I still hit failure unless I force `pip install --upgrade --force-reinstall tokenizers==0.11.6 --no-binary :none:`
Mia: thanks. Kevin, please pin the PR with `#urgent` and link to the CI job: https://ci.redwood/infer/8721
OpsBot: deploy-bot: created staging rollout `inference-stg-rollback` at 2026-03-20T14:12:00Z for service inference-staging:v1.2.3-rollback
Sanjay: what about CVE handling? If tokenizers has a vulnerability that can be exploited at parse-time, we should check logs for suspicious inputs and audit KMS usage in the last 24h. Not high probability, but compliance wants the check.
Mia: I ran a quick grep; no suspicious payloads in request logs. KMS audit shows normal decrypt rates — no unexpected principals.
Jordan: good. After rollback we should coordinate with research/infra to rebuild wheels for our supported platforms (linux-x86_64, linux-arm64, macos-x86_64) so we don't depend on upstream prebuilt wheels that break ABI.
Kevin: agree. For immediate fix I'll: revert poetry.lock, add constraints, add a CI gate on `macos-latest` and `arm64` with allowed-failures flagged off, and add a `pip wheel` rebuild job.
Mia: priority = P1 until 18:00 PT. If rollback passes staging smoke, we'll merge and cut a prod rollback window. Jordan, please monitor model quality metrics and evals once staging is up.
Jordan: will do. Also schedule a follow-up meeting tomorrow to plan phased upgrade to the patched tokenizer with full regression suite.
Sanjay: after we merge, let's add a follow-up ticket to update our dependency policy: require wheel ABI checks + cross-platform wheels before auto-approving transformers/tokenizers PRs.
Mia: created the hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/987 — includes lock rollback + `pyproject` constraints + CI job change. Marked `security: true`.
Kevin: CI green on linux, mac still flaky — digging into mac wheel caching.
OpsBot: ci-bot: job 8721 updated status -> queued -> running -> failing (macos-latest)
Mia: if macos keeps failing and it's blocking, we can merge with `ci:macos` approval from eng-plat + signal to ops to hold prod rollout for 30m, but prefer to get green.
Jordan: note for postmortem: better dependabot rules to avoid simultaneous transformers+tokenizers bumps without human review.
Mia: agreed. I'll notify `#incidents` if we must rollback prod. For now I'm going to merge once linux+staging smoke pass. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
